title: Lazy LINQ
sub: A query is a recipe, not a result
cards/0/body: The line var q = numbers.Where(…).Select(…) computes nothing. It only builds a chain. The work starts when something enumerates the result: foreach, ToList, Count, First…
cards/1/task: Step through the query. Watch the order in which Where and Select are called and where the query stops.
cards/2/q: Why were only four of the six numbers read?
cards/2/options/0: Take(2) got two elements and stopped asking for more
cards/2/explain: The chain pulls elements one at a time. Once it has enough, it stops pulling.
cards/3/q: In what order do the calls happen?
cards/3/options/0: Each element goes through the whole chain before the next is taken: Where(1), Where(5), Select(5)…
cards/3/options/1: Where for all of them first, then Select for all
cards/4/body: Since the query runs when it is enumerated, it sees the data as of enumeration, not as of when you wrote it.
cards/5/explain: 2, 3 and 10 — the query ran after the Add.
cards/6/q: What triggers the query to run? Select all.
cards/6/explain: Where and Select only add links to the chain.
